best_parts: node p5_t7a and p5_t7b: each TG18 wrong set maps to one distinct wrong model (imaging in the first set; bedside signs already definite), with a sure_note
node p8_t5b: tender mass tempts the learner to read 'non-tender' as the only qualifier; refutation names the jaundice qualifier and the inflammation reading
node p1_t4: tempting-then-refute feedback that names colic's steady course and the 6-hour clock
flaws: node p3: the key 'Outlet blocked only briefly, wall not inflamed' is the longest option and the only one stating the wall logic, so it is findable by form (DP1)
nodes p1..p9: nine probes in a row with almost no explanation node between them; the learner gets one-line feedback and no consolidated mechanism until the end, which is heavy for a tired learner
node p2 option 'Infected bile with no stone at all' (TR23): tenuous as a wrong model for the cause question, closer to a different topic than the trap it claims

best_parts: node pain_explain: a short explain node after the first correct commit (calculous stone plus wall inflammation versus transient block), then re-probed in pain2_case; ask, explain, re-ask
node sign_explain: clinical clues (Murphy's absent in elderly and diabetics, Boas' sign, shoulder-tip pain) make the segment feel like a real clinic moment
node pain_t4a and cv_t5a: sure_note plus 'Show me why' agency, giving a learner who was confident two routes into the explanation
flaws: node cv_case: the only option starting 'It does not apply' is the key; the two traps both begin 'It applies', so the key is findable by form (DP1)
node cv_recog: the key is the only option with a condition ('In jaundice'), so the qualifier gives it away; a learner who ignores the law's content still picks it
node pain_why and cv_why: 'Show me why' largely restates the answer ('Here is the answer') rather than giving a second, different explanation

best_parts: node open: two-patient contrast (Patient A afebrile, 3 hours; Patient B 30 hours, fever, Murphy's) is a strong, quick opening probe with a clear clock
node contrast: side-by-side explain of colic versus cholecystitis is a crisp second explanation that a tired learner can scan
node tg_a: trap 'Two systemic signs with no local sign' is a distinct wrong model from the imaging-first trap, and is well refuted in tg_a_t3
flaws: TR4 is probed only once in this segment (node open); there is no second TR4 probe in a different form, so recovery on the trap is not tested here
TR5 is probed only once (node cv, vignette form) and no re-test in another form, against the two-form rule; the stem 'He is not jaundiced' makes the key easy to reach
node tg_b_t2: 'Not diagnosable until imaging is done' is partly dominated by tg_b_t1 for a learner with surface knowledge, so one trap feels like filler

merge_ideas: b's pain_explain and sign_explain after a's full probe ladder: keep a's p5/p6 TG18 set probes and sure_notes, insert b's short explain node after the first commit
open (c) as the first probe, then b's pain_case re-probe in a different form, so TR4 is tested twice in one segment with a contrast explanation between
a's three-form TR5 ladder (p7 recognition, p8 vignette, p9 recognition) with b's 'Show me why' agency and c's shorter cv probe for a fast lane
